introduction.text: Forte Casilina is one of Rome’s 15 19th‑century forts, built between 1877 and 1891 to defend the city. It played a role in the city’s military history and is now the focus of restoration projects that aim to return it to public use.

history.description: Forte Casilina was part of Rome's fortification ring built between 1871 and 1885.
Construction of Forte Casilina began in 1881 and was completed in 1882.
The fort was named Forte Casilina by royal decree on 1 November 1882.
After the war, the fort served as a storage facility for air squadron logistics until May 1965.
During World War II, the fort was used by German troops stationed at the nearby airport.
Presently, projects are underway to restore the fort for public use.

design.description: The fort’s layout is a trapezoidal shape with a single entrance on the longer side, a dry moat, and internal service rooms.
